items.name: Casa de la Vall
items.body:
A 16th-century stone manor that served as Andorra's seat of government (the Consell General) until 2011, now a small museum on Carrer de la Vall in the Barri Antic. {{fact:casa-de-la-vall-5-eur}} general admission, €2.50 reduced; a €1.50 guided-tour supplement is available with advance booking.

Visits are reservation-only — there's no walk-up admission. Book by phone (+376 839760) or email (museusandorra@gmail.com) before you travel; same-day slots aren't guaranteed. The visits page has the request form.

items.name: Sant Esteve Church
items.body: An 11th–12th century Romanesque church on Plaça Bisbe Benlloch, remodelled in 1940 by modernist architect Josep Puig i Cadafalch. Still an active parish church, with the largest Romanesque apse in Andorra and a 12th-century polychrome wooden beam inside. Free entry; not wheelchair accessible.

items.name: Església de Santa Coloma
items.kicker: Andorra la Vella's oldest church, no reservation needed
items.body:
An 8th–9th century pre-Romanesque nave — the oldest church in the Andorra la Vella parish — with a distinctive 12th-century circular Lombard bell tower, one of the last of its kind in the Pyrenees. Open Jan–May and Oct–Dec, Tuesday–Saturday 10:00–14:00 and 15:00–18:00, closed Sunday and Monday; €7 admission, €3.50 reduced.

It stands on Carrer Major in the Santa Coloma quarter, not in the Barri Antic. The Line 1 bus (Escaldes-Engordany ↔ Sant Julià de Lòria) runs past it; ⚠ check the current timetable at bus.ad, or take a taxi.

The self-guided audioguide visit needs no advance booking — only the guided tour does. That makes it the fallback when Casa de la Vall's reservation slots don't line up. It keeps the same Sunday and Monday closures, so on this trip it works Thursday, Friday or Saturday only.

The church interior is not adapted for reduced mobility. The adjoining Espai Columba has step-free access, a shop and toilets.

items.name: Barri Antic
items.body:
The capital's original core dates to the 11th century, taking shape around the first granite houses and lanes cut to the slope. Cobbled streets run off Carrer Major and Carrer del Pui into a handful of small squares.

Small enough to walk in under an hour, but worth spreading across the trip: it holds Casa de la Vall, Sant Esteve and most of the old-town restaurants in one compact radius.

items.name: Llac d'Engolasters
items.kicker: Andorra's easiest signed lake route — from Encamp, out and back
items.body:
The official signed route to the lake starts in Encamp, in front of the Automobile Museum — not at the lake itself. It runs out and back: 1.9 km, rated Easy, +350 m on the way up and −45 m coming down, about 1 hour 15 minutes up and 45 minutes back.

The path crosses waterways and a couple of roads, joins the GR-11's red-and-white waymarks, and finishes at the 178-metre Engolasters dam and its reservoir lake.

The trail authority names June to September as this route's season, stretching to May–October when weather and terrain allow. November falls outside that window. Treat it as a conditions-dependent morning rather than a fixed plan — ice on the shaded stretches is the usual reason to call it off.

items.name: Museu Nacional de l'Automòbil
items.kicker: At the Engolasters trailhead — the indoor half of day three
items.body:
Andorra's national car museum stands on Avinguda de Joan Martí in Encamp, directly opposite the start of the signed Engolasters route. Open October to December, Tuesday–Saturday 10:00–14:00 and 15:00–18:00, closed Sunday and Monday. {{fact:automobile-museum-5-eur}} general admission, €2.50 reduced.

Its value on this trip is the shared bus stop: if the trail is iced over, the Encamp day still has somewhere to go. Line 2 (Encamp) and Line 4 (Pas de la Casa) both stop for it.

items.claim: Roc del Quer's cliffside viewpoint is an easy add-on to a Canillo day trip.
items.correction: The mirador itself is reachable only by car, via a single mountain road (CS-240, km 6.5) with no bus service — it only works with a rental car or taxi, which is why this car-free itinerary skips it. It's open daily year-round (9:30–19:00, weather permitting), so access — not the season — is the actual blocker.

items.claim: Casa de la Vall is a walk-in museum like the Barri Antic's other small sights.
items.correction: Admission is reservation-only — there's no walk-up entry. Book by phone (+376 839760) or email (museusandorra@gmail.com) before you travel; same-day slots aren't guaranteed.

items.claim: Andorra's hiking trails run on a normal spring-through-autumn season.
items.correction: Andorra's own trail authority recommends routes above 1,700 m only between the end of June and the end of September, and says the season stretches to May–October only where weather and terrain allow. That upper bound is October, not November — so even an Easy valley route like Llac d'Engolasters is a check-the-conditions call on the morning, not a fixed item on the plan.

items.claim: Andorra is inside the EU/Schengen area, so a stop here counts as part of a Schengen trip.
items.correction: Andorra is outside both the EU and the Schengen area. It's reachable only by first crossing into Spain or France, so the entry rules that actually govern the trip are those two countries' Schengen rules, not a separate Andorran one — and a multi-entry Schengen visa (if one is required) matters more here than almost anywhere else in Europe.
